issues.t: Airbag light from spilled drinks or seat wiring contact
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and stays on, often after a drink was spilled near the center console.
issues.why: Liquid can drip through the parking brake opening onto the airbag computer connector, and on some cars seat material can rub the side airbag wiring. Either can stop the airbags from deploying. Hyundai recalled these cars and added a protective cover.
issues.next: Treat a lit airbag light as a safety problem. Check your VIN for both recalls and have a dealer fix it soon.

issues.t: Brake hose can leak fluid
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake warning light, or fluid wetness near a wheel.
issues.why: Certain front brake hoses could leak brake fluid, which reduces stopping power. Hyundai recalled the cars to replace them.
issues.next: Do not keep driving with a soft pedal. Check your VIN for the brake hose recall and have the brakes inspected right away.

issues.t: Front lower control arms rust through
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering steering, or a front wheel that sits at an odd angle. Visible heavy rust on the arms.
issues.why: In areas that use a lot of road salt, the front lower control arms can corrode and thin out until they crack near the ball joint. Hyundai recalled these cars to inspect and replace the arms.
issues.next: Stop driving if the front end suddenly feels loose. Check your VIN for the control arm recall and have the arms inspected.

issues.t: Brake light switch failure
issues.sym: Brake lights that do not come on, cruise control that will not cancel when braking, or a shifter that will not leave Park (or leaves Park without pressing the brake). Warning lights may flicker on.
issues.why: The brake light switch can work only some of the time. Several other systems rely on that switch. Hyundai issued multiple recalls to replace it.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. If they are not working, get the switch replaced right away and check your VIN for the open recalls.

issues.t: Front airbag sensor recalls
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, or no warning at all. The passenger airbag may deploy when it should not, or the driver airbag may deploy harder than intended.
issues.why: Faults in the passenger occupant sensing and the driver seat position sensor could make the front airbags behave wrongly in a crash. Hyundai recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both airbag recalls and have a dealer complete them. Get any airbag light checked soon.

issues.t: ABS module can short and start a fire
issues.sym: ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from under the hood, even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the anti-lock brake module and cause an electrical short. Hyundai recalled these cars and added a relay that cuts power to the module when the car is off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this fire recall. Park outside and away from buildings until the repair is done.

issues.t: Clicking or clunk from the steering column
issues.sym: A click, clunk, or light knock felt in the steering wheel when turning, mostly at low speeds and when parking.
issues.why: A rubber coupler inside the electric power steering column wears out. Hyundai extended the warranty on this part by bulletin.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the steering coupler and ask whether your car still falls under the extended coverage.

issues.t: ABS module can short and start a fire
issues.sym: ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from the engine bay, even when the car is parked.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the anti-lock brake control unit and cause an electrical short. Hyundai recalled these cars and told owners to park outside until fixed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the ABS fire recall. Park outdoors away from buildings until the fix is done.

issues.t: Piston slap and cylinder wall scuffing
issues.sym: A ticking or knocking from the engine, loudest when cold, sometimes with a check engine light or rising oil use.
issues.why: Pistons can rock in their bores and scuff the cylinder walls. Hyundai released bulletins with a test procedure and extended warranty coverage for short-block and long-block damage.
issues.next: Have a dealer run the engine noise test from the bulletins and ask about the extended engine coverage. Keep oil changes on time.

issues.t: Transmission speed sensor faults
issues.sym: Check engine light, harsh or odd shifting, or the transmission going into a limp mode.
issues.why: The input and output speed sensors or their wiring connectors can fail. A Hyundai bulletin covers checking the harness and fitting new sensors.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask the shop to follow Hyundai bulletin 13-AT-014 before replacing the whole transmission.

issues.t: Key-start cars easy to steal
issues.sym: A broken steering column cover or ignition cylinder, a car that will not start with the key, or a car that is missing.
issues.why: Many key-start versions lack an engine immobilizer, so thieves can start them without the key. Hyundai offers a free anti-theft software update and steering wheel lock through service campaigns.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for the anti-theft software campaign and get it installed. Use a steering wheel lock in the meantime.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing failure
issues.sym: A knock that rises with engine speed, oil pressure or check engine light, stalling, or loss of power.
issues.why: The connecting rod bearings in this engine can wear and fail, which can seize the engine. Hyundai added knock-detection software and extended engine coverage under a class settlement.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear a new knock. Have a dealer confirm the knock-detection software update is done and ask about the extended engine warranty.

issues.t: Thermostat stuck open
issues.sym: Check engine light, a temperature gauge that stays low, and weak cabin heat.
issues.why: The thermostat can open too early, so the engine takes too long to warm up. Hyundai issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Have the code read and the thermostat replaced. It is not urgent, but fuel economy and heat suffer.

issues.t: Misfire with check engine light
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, or shaking under acceleration.
issues.why: Some 2.0L engines set misfire codes that Hyundai addressed with a dedicated repair bulletin.
issues.next: If the light is flashing, drive gently and get it checked soon. Ask the shop to follow Hyundai bulletin 20-FL-001H.

issues.t: Dual-clutch shudder at low speed
issues.sym: Shaking or vibration when pulling away or creeping in traffic, and jerky low-speed shifts.
issues.why: The 7-speed dry dual-clutch transmission can vibrate at low speeds. Hyundai issued bulletins and updated clutch parts and software.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the dual-clutch bulletins and software updates.

issues.t: Oil burning from faulty piston rings
issues.sym: Oil level dropping between changes, blue smoke, engine knocking, or an oil pressure light.
issues.why: Piston oil rings that were not heat-treated correctly can chip and damage the cylinders. This can lead to heavy oil use, engine seizure, and in some cases a fire. Hyundai recalled these engines.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the piston ring recall. Stop driving if the engine knocks or the oil light comes on.

issues.t: CVT (IVT) check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission codes, sometimes with poor acceleration.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission can set fault codes that Hyundai fixes with a control software update, and in some cases a new transmission.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and apply the transmission software update from the bulletin.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioner can burst in a crash
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The danger shows only when the belt tightener fires in a crash or airbag deployment.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners can rupture instead of tightening the belt smoothly, sending metal pieces into the cabin. Hyundai recalled the cars to fit a redesigned part.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the pretensioner recall and book the repair as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: CVT oil pressure sensor fault
issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: A faulty oil pressure sensor in the continuously variable transmission can set codes. Hyundai's bulletin says to replace the sensor rather than the whole transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about Hyundai bulletin 23-AT-010H.

issues.t: Fuel tank can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell, a wet tank, or fuel on the ground under the rear of the car.
issues.why: A fault in the vapor recovery system can pull too much vacuum on the fuel tank until it cracks.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Hyundai dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers quit mid-sweep or will not turn on, often in heavy rain or snow.
issues.why: The circuit breaker contacts in the wiper motor were contaminated at the factory.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips from leaking solenoid seals (recall)
issues.sym: The engine revs but the car is slow to move or pick up speed, and shifts feel soft or delayed.
issues.why: Seals on the pressure control solenoids break down and leak fluid pressure inside the transmission, so the clutches slip.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Engine stalls at low speed from airflow sensor wiring (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out now and then while slowing down or creeping in traffic, and usually restarts.
issues.why: Engine vibration can break the connection in the wiring to the mass airflow sensor.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve may not close (recall)
issues.sym: Normally nothing. Fuel can spill if the car rolls over in a crash.
issues.why: A valve on the fuel tank may not seal as it should.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Hose clamp can puncture the fuel tank (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel dripping near the rear of the car.
issues.why: A clamp on a vapor hose was installed pointing at the fuel tank and can rub or poke a hole in it.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Hyundai dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor can mistake a child seat for an adult (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag indicator shows the airbag is on with a child seat in the front seat.
issues.why: The seat sensing system can classify a child seat wrongly, so the airbag could fire when it should stay off.
issues.next: Keep children in the back seat and have a Hyundai dealer complete the free recall.

issues.t: Steering rack inner joints can crack (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: A knock or looseness in the steering, or the car suddenly not responding to the wheel.
issues.why: The inner ball joints of the steering rack may have internal cracks, and a tie rod can pull apart.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until a Hyundai dealer confirms by VIN that this recall was done.

issues.t: Front seat back recliner weld may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal use. The seat back could give way in a crash.
issues.why: The recliner mechanisms on some front seats were not welded properly.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: A blank or black screen when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: The circuit board inside the rear camera can be damaged.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Steering wheel emblem can fly off when the airbag fires (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal driving.
issues.why: The badge on the driver airbag cover may not be welded on securely and can hit the driver when the airbag opens.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Idle stop oil pump controller can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, sometimes with warning lights, even when parked.
issues.why: The controller for the electric oil pump used by the idle stop and go system can have damaged parts that overheat.
issues.next: Park outside and away from buildings until a Hyundai dealer has done the free recall repair.

issues.t: EGR valve short can cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: A check engine light followed by a sudden loss of power while driving.
issues.why: An electrical short inside the exhaust gas recirculation valve can make the car lose drive power.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Hyundai dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Wheel lug nuts or front strut fasteners may be loose (recalls)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunk from a wheel, vibration, or steering that feels loose.
issues.why: Some cars left the factory with wheel nuts or front strut fasteners that were not tightened fully. A wheel could come off or steering control could be lost.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Hyundai dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Side impact sensors may be assembled wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing; possibly an airbag warning light.
issues.why: The crash sensors in the center door pillars may not be assembled correctly, so side airbags could fire late.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Hyundai or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Side air bag sensors may be faulty (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows up day to day, but the side air bags may stay shut in a side impact.
issues.why: The two side satellite sensors were built incorrectly, so they may not tell the air bags to fire.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the VIN and replace both sensors; the repair is free under recall.

issues.t: Passenger air bag can switch itself off with an adult in the seat (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag off light stays lit even with a grown adult sitting there.
issues.why: The seat occupant sensor can read an adult as an infant and disable the air bag.
issues.next: Get the sensor reprogrammed; it is free under recall and the air bag will not protect that seat until it is done.

issues.t: Fuel pump can make low pressure and stall the engine (recalls)
issues.sym: Hard starting, stumbling under load, or the engine quits and will not restart right away.
issues.why: Some in-tank fuel pumps do not build enough pressure to feed the injectors.
issues.next: Have the pump replaced before it leaves you stranded; it is free under recall on affected cars.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The wheel suddenly goes heavy, usually with a steering warning light.
issues.why: A fault in the electric power steering control unit can shut the assist off.
issues.next: Have the control unit updated right away; heavy steering at low speed makes parking lot turns and sudden swerves hard.

issues.t: Front coil spring can rust through and break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or bang from a front corner, the car sitting lower on one side, or a cut tire.
issues.why: Road salt corrodes the front springs, and a broken coil end can dig into the tire.
issues.next: Have the springs inspected soon, especially in salt states; replacement is free under recall on affected cars.

issues.t: Stability control can brake a wheel on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The car pulls or slows by itself, often with the stability control light on.
issues.why: A faulty sensor signal makes the stability control system apply a brake when it should not.
issues.next: Get the sensors checked and the calibration updated promptly; unexpected braking is a crash risk.

issues.t: The 12-volt power outlet can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or heat discoloration around the cigarette lighter socket.
issues.why: The outlet can get hot when something is plugged in and drawing current for a long stretch.
issues.next: Unplug accessories and have the recall harness installed, which feeds the outlet through a protected circuit.

issues.t: Headliner bracket can be pushed loose by the curtain air bag (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see; it only matters in a crash when the roof air bag deploys.
issues.why: A bracket above the headliner can be driven out of place as the curtain air bag inflates.
issues.next: Have the recall adhesive strips added at the dealer; it is a free, quick repair.

issues.t: Worn brake pedal pad keeps the brake lights on (recalls)
issues.sym: Brake lights glow all the time, cruise control will not set, and the shifter may move out of Park without the brake pressed.
issues.why: A small stopper pad on the brake pedal crumbles, so the switch behind the pedal never releases.
issues.next: Get the pad replaced soon; a car that can leave Park without the brake pedal can roll away.

issues.t: Trunk latch can block the inside release (recall)
issues.sym: The glow-in-the-dark release handle inside the trunk does not open the lid.
issues.why: The latch base can keep the emergency inside release from working.
issues.next: Have the latch base replaced free under recall, and keep children away from an unrepaired trunk.

issues.t: Driver air bag may not inflate properly (recalls)
issues.sym: No warning at all; the air bag may inflate weakly or only part way in a crash.
issues.why: Some driver air bag modules were built with a missing seal or missing propellant material.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the VIN and replace the module; it is free under recall.

issues.t: Brake booster can fail and lengthen stopping distance (recall)
issues.sym: The pedal feels hard and the car takes much longer to stop.
issues.why: The brake booster can lose its assist, leaving you pushing the pedal with leg force alone.
issues.next: Have the booster replaced right away; stopping distances grow a lot without assist.

issues.t: Steering motor connector can fail and kill power assist (recall)
issues.sym: The wheel goes heavy, usually with a steering warning light on the dash.
issues.why: A damaged connector at the electric steering motor can interrupt the assist.
issues.next: Have the steering motor replaced under recall before driving it much further.

issues.t: Wheel lug nuts or ball joint bolts may be loose (recalls)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a corner, a wobble you can feel in the wheel, or a wheel that looks out of line.
issues.why: Right rear lug nuts and front lower ball joint fasteners were not tightened to spec at the factory.
issues.next: Have both checked and tightened right away; a loose wheel or ball joint can come apart while driving.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or water leaks at the edge of the windshield.
issues.why: The adhesive bead was not applied correctly, so the glass may not stay put in a crash or rollover.
issues.next: Have the dealer remove and reset the windshield under recall; the glass also backs up the passenger air bag.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips and can stop pulling
issues.sym: The engine revs up without the car speeding up, shifts come late or with a thump, and in bad cases the car will not move in Drive at all. Owners of these years report it most often at middling to high mileage.
issues.why: The automatic used in this generation is hard on its clutches and bands, and old fluid that has never been changed makes it worse. Once the friction material wears away, the pump and valve body get fed with debris and the unit loses pressure.
issues.next: Get the fluid level and condition checked right away and the codes read before any more driving than you need. Slipping that has gone on for a while usually means a rebuild or a replacement unit rather than a service.
